_comment: Template for config.json, which lives in the LXC next to docker-compose.yml
and is never in git. It is mounted read-only; after an edit, recreate the
container (docker compose up -d --force-recreate), because a single-file
bind mount keeps the old file's inode when an editor replaces it.
rois and align.reference are ONE MATCHED PAIR: every ROI is a pixel
rectangle in the reference frame. Move the camera and both are redone
together -- see docs/operations.md.
Itron Gallus 2000 G4. 8 drums behind glass: five black (whole m3), three
red (0.001 m3). WHITE DIGITS ON DARK DRUMS, the opposite of most meters
the networks were trained on; inverting them was measured and changed
nothing, so it is not the thing to reach for first.
The camera frames seven drums -- 0 2 2 6 1 | 7 2 -- and the 0.001 drum
is out of shot, so the meter is read as seven drums with two decimals.
Applied to every frame first. flip: none | horizontal | vertical |
both; rotate: 0 | 90 | 180 | 270 clockwise; deskew: fine levelling
in degrees, positive counter-clockwise. A tilted row cannot be fitted
by axis-aligned boxes, and the model reads a digit's height in its
box as PHASE -- level the row here before placing ROIs.
ORB matches every frame against the reference and warps it back onto
it, so a nudged bracket costs nothing. The min_*/max_* bars are
digits.align_gate(): a transform that exists is not one that can be
trusted. A missing reference or a failed alignment REJECTS the read --
fixed rectangles over an uncorrected frame give a confident wrong
number, which is worse than none.

_comment_reading: counter_type jump: each whole-number drum snaps forward when the drum
to its right completes a turn, so every drum is rounded on its own.
The wrong value corrupts digits the model read correctly.
report_decimals 2: do not coarsen this. max_delta must exceed the
meter's 0.5 m3 per 5 min plus one published step; at whole m3 a
misread units drum (+1 m3) would sit inside the allowance.
round_last_drum_down: a last drum caught mid-roll publishes the digit
LEAVING the window, from 0.7 of the way through; never across 9 -> 0.

_comment: max_delta 0.6 m3 per 300 s, scaled by the time since the last
accepted read: a G4 at its rated maximum only reaches 0.5. It is
there to catch a misread digit, not to police the boiler.
tolerance_down 0.0: the Energy sensor is total_increasing, and a
decrease of more than 10% is taken as a meter reset that retyping
does not undo. Never accept one.
min_confidence skips the last drum by position; on seven drums that
is the published 0.01 drum, so it gets its own floor.
The frames of one wake must agree. The camera sends two; one frame
alone is refused.
The token is METERCAM_HA_TOKEN in .env, never here.
An accepted reading is written to the camera's own helper;
sensor.gas_meter_reading (the Energy dashboard's gas source) takes the
higher of that and the hand-typed helper -- see
HomeAssistant/config/packages/gas_meter.yaml. The prevalue is the same
helper; while it is 0 (just created) or Home Assistant is restarting,
the service's own last accepted reading stands in.
